walkthroughs.body_html:
Religion, Peace & Conflict through a Study of Islam (Spec B) — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religion, Peace & Conflict through a Study of Islam (Spec B) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religion, Peace & Conflict through a Study of Islam (Spec B).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
